title: How Does Your Phone Know Which Way Is Up?
sources: Make Tech Easier, 'How phone accelerometers detect orientation' and 'How a phone accelerometer works': a MEMS accelerometer is a silicon chip smaller than a grain of rice; a tiny proof mass hangs on silicon springs with comb-like fingers interleaved with fixed fingers; tilting lets gravity shift the mass by a few nanometres, changing the capacitance between the fingers, which the circuit measures to know the direction of gravity

Edinburgh Napier University IoT notes, 'Accelerometer' (bdavison.napier.ac.uk/iot/Notes/components/accelerometer): capacitive MEMS accelerometer = proof mass on springs between fixed plates; displacement changes capacitance; at rest it measures gravity, so it gives tilt/orientation

NXP application note AN3461 'Tilt Sensing Using Linear Accelerometers': orientation is computed from the gravity components on the X/Y/Z axes; when the device lies flat, gravity is entirely on the Z axis (through the screen) and the X/Y readings give no up/down direction
Android Developers Blog, 'One Screen Turn Deserves Another' (Sept 2010): screen rotation is decided from the accelerometer / orientation sensors relative to gravity

Wikipedia 'iPhone (1st generation)' / Apple 2007 press release 'Apple Reinvents the Phone with iPhone': the original iPhone included an accelerometer that rotated the display between portrait and landscape

lines.text: How does your phone know when to flip the screen sideways?
lines.caps: HOW *DOES | YOUR *PHONE | *KNOW | WHEN TO *FLIP | THE SCREEN *SIDEWAYS?

lines.text: Well, inside is a tiny chip called an accelerometer,
smaller than a grain of rice.
In there, a little block of silicon hangs on springs,
lines.caps: IN *THERE | A LITTLE *BLOCK | OF *SILICON | HANGS ON *SPRINGS

lines.text: with comb-like fingers next to fixed ones.
When you tilt the phone, gravity tugs that block,
so the gaps between the fingers change by a few nanometers.
lines.caps: SO THE *GAPS | BETWEEN THE *FINGERS | *CHANGE BY | A FEW *NANOMETERS

lines.text: The chip feels that as a change in electricity,
so it knows which way gravity is pulling,
and the screen turns to match.
Here's the twist: lay your phone flat on a table,
lines.caps: HERE'S THE *TWIST | LAY YOUR *PHONE | *FLAT | ON A *TABLE

lines.text: and gravity points straight through the screen,
so it can't tell which side is up, and won't rotate.
lines.caps: SO IT *CAN'T | *TELL | WHICH *SIDE | IS *UP | AND WON'T *ROTATE
